directAnswer: You can extract ZIP files on a Mac by double-clicking the file or using the built-in Archive Utility.
summary: Extracting ZIP files on macOS is straightforward and can be done using the Finder or Terminal.

sections.heading: Extracting ZIP Files Using Finder
sections.body: The simplest way to extract ZIP files is through the Finder. Just locate the ZIP file, double-click it, and the contents will be extracted to the same directory.

sections.heading: Extracting ZIP Files Using Terminal
sections.body: For advanced users, you can also use the Terminal. Open Terminal and use the command 'unzip <filename>.zip' to extract the files.

steps.title: Locate the ZIP file
steps.detail: Open Finder and navigate to the folder containing the ZIP file you want to extract.

steps.title: Extract the files
steps.detail: Double-click the ZIP file to automatically extract it using Archive Utility.

steps.title: Using Terminal (optional)
steps.detail: Open Terminal, type 'unzip', followed by a space, and drag the ZIP file into the Terminal window to auto-fill the path. Press Enter to extract.

faqs.question: What if the ZIP file is password protected?
faqs.answer: You'll need to use a third-party tool like The Unarchiver or command-line tools that support password-protected ZIP files.

faqs.question: Can I extract ZIP files to a different location?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can drag the extracted folder to your desired location after extraction.

faqs.question: What if the ZIP file doesn't open?
faqs.answer: The file may be corrupted or not a valid ZIP file. Try downloading it again.

caveats: Some older versions of macOS may have different default applications for handling ZIP files.
